We need answer JSON only. Need produce declaration/implementation/supporting_objects. Need implement FB_Task with interface exact. Need maybe helper DUTs? Likely no supporting objects needed. But requirement "Define referenced DUTs" none. Could include no helper. Need ensure CODESYS 3.5 ST syntax. Declaration is FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task followed by VAR sections; omit END_FUNCTION_BLOCK. Need include initial values. Outputs PumpA PumpB LeadA. Internal state variables maybe LeadA_State, previous_demand, served, PumpCmdA, PumpCmdB, scanDemand, scanFaultA, scanFaultB, fallingEdge. Interface exact names types. Output LeadA bool initial true? In CODESYS output vars can have initial values? Declaration: VAR_OUTPUT PumpA : BOOL := FALSE; etc, LeadA : BOOL := TRUE; yes. Inputs no init. Internal previous_demand BOOL := FALSE; served BOOL := FALSE; LeadA_State BOOL := TRUE; PumpCmdA etc.

Implementation per stage. Need carefully handle falling edge and served. At scan:
scanDemand := Demand; scanFaultA:=FaultA; scanFaultB:=FaultB;
fallingEdge := previous_demand AND NOT scanDemand;

IF NOT scanDemand THEN
 PumpCmdA := FALSE; PumpCmdB := FALSE;
 IF fallingEdge AND served THEN LeadA_State := NOT LeadA_State; END_IF;
 served := FALSE;
ELSE
 // select healthy
 IF LeadA_State THEN
   IF NOT scanFaultA THEN
     PumpCmdA := TRUE; PumpCmdB := FALSE;
   ELSIF NOT scanFaultB THEN
     PumpCmdA := FALSE; PumpCmdB := TRUE;
   ELSE
     PumpCmdA := FALSE; PumpCmdB := FALSE;
   END_IF;
 ELSE
   IF NOT scanFaultB THEN
     PumpCmdA := FALSE; PumpCmdB := TRUE;
   ELSIF NOT scanFaultA THEN
     PumpCmdA := TRUE; PumpCmdB := FALSE;
   ELSE
     ...
   END_IF;
 END_IF;
 IF PumpCmdA OR PumpCmdB THEN served := TRUE; END_IF;
END_IF;
previous_demand := scanDemand;
PumpA := PumpCmdA; PumpB := PumpCmdB; LeadA := LeadA_State;

Need consider safety priority: faulted pumps never run. In fallback branches ensure don't run faulted. If lead A healthy run A even if B fault, yes. If lead A faulted and B healthy run B. If both healthy and LeadA true run A only. P2 etc: (!Demand | FaultA) -> !PumpA. If Demand true FaultA true PumpA false. Good. P4 Demand & LeadA & !FaultA -> PumpA. Our LeadA output equals LeadA_State post transition. On Demand true no falling edge so LeadA stable. Good. P5 Demand & !LeadA & !FaultB -> PumpB. Our LeadA_State false, if B healthy run B. Good. P8 Demand FaultA !FaultB -> PumpB. Our if LeadA true A fault -> B; if LeadA false B healthy -> B. Good. P9 similarly.

Edge toggle: completedServed := previous_demand (reference state demand?) AND NOT Demand AND served. We use fallingEdge AND served. On falling edge with served true toggle. P6 G(completedServed -> LeadA <-> !qLeadA). qLeadA previous observed output. Since LeadA output post toggle. For demand false scan following served, output LeadA = NOT prior. Good. If multiple false scans, fallingEdge false, no toggle. served reset false. LeadA held. P7 for !completedServed hold. Our on Demand true LeadA unchanged. On false no edge unchanged. On falling edge but served false unchanged. Good. Potential issue: "Demand = FALSE: if previous_demand = TRUE AND served = TRUE toggle LeadA; reset served". We do. previous_demand update after. Good.

Need maybe use R_TRIG? No.

Need decide whether to include helper DUTs. None. supporting_objects [].

Need ensure declaration format valid. They said "declaration is CODESYS FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task followed by all VAR sections; omit END_FUNCTION_BLOCK." So string:
"FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task\nVAR_INPUT\n    Demand : BOOL;\n...\nEND_VAR\nVAR_OUTPUT\n...\nEND_VAR\nVAR\n...\nEND_VAR"

Need include output initial values? CODESYS allows initialization for VAR_OUTPUT? In CODESYS, variables can be initialized in declaration. E.g. VAR_OUTPUT x : BOOL := FALSE; END_VAR. Should be okay. For FB output LeadA initial true. Could also initialize in implementation? But requirement initial pre-state; better declarations. However if output initialized in declaration, each online reset sets. Fine.

Need no Markdown. Return JSON object with keys. Implementation string body alone. Could include comments? okay. Need perhaps avoid semicolons after END_IF? CODESYS ST uses semicolons after statements but not after END_IF. Fine.

Potential nuance: "LeadA reflects post-transition preference" output. We assign at end. Internal LeadA_State initialized true. Good.

Potential nuance: "previous_demand tracks I[k].Demand on every scan." We update at end. At scan 0 previous false. Good.

Potential nuance: served := FALSE on Demand false after toggle. If demand false first scan after served true, toggle. Good.

Potential nuance: If Demand true and both fault, served remains from previous? Wait served is latch across demand episode. If both fault while Demand true, no pump runs; served should not be set true. If served was already true earlier in same demand episode, it remains true (because we only set true, not clear in demand). Then if fault occurs later in same episode, served remains true from earlier service. At falling edge, toggles. Is that correct? "If either pump runs on this scan, mark served := TRUE." Served is episode memory: once any pump runs during episode, episode served. If later both fault, still served true. That is likely correct. Our code on Demand true with no pump does not clear served, so retains. Good. If previous episode served true, and demand false clears. Fine.

Need maybe implement as state machine using CASE? But simple if. No timers.

Potential compilation issues: Variable named "served" okay. "previous_demand" okay. "LeadA_State". Output LeadA. No conflict.

Need include internal scanDemand etc? Yes. Could use inputs directly but plan says sample. We'll include.

Would there be issue with initializing VAR_OUTPUT? In CODESYS, for function block, output var init may be allowed? Yes. But sometimes output variables are not allowed initial values? IEC permits. CODESYS permits initialization of any variable in VAR sections. Good.

Need perhaps include `VAR_INPUT` names exactly Demand, FaultA, FaultB. Outputs PumpA, PumpB, LeadA.

Could there be a request for supporting_objects to define DUTs? They say "Define referenced DUTs." None referenced. Return [].

Let's craft final JSON valid. Need escape newlines. Use JSON string with \n. Ensure no unescaped quotes. Implementation body. Could use `NOT` and `AND` uppercase. ST is case-insensitive.

Implementation:
"scanDemand := Demand;\nscanFaultA := FaultA;\nscanFaultB := FaultB;\nfallingEdge := previous_demand AND NOT scanDemand;\n\nIF NOT scanDemand THEN\n    PumpCmdA := FALSE;\n    PumpCmdB := FALSE;\n    IF fallingEdge AND served THEN\n        LeadA_State := NOT LeadA_State;\n    END_IF;\n    served := FALSE;\nELSE\n    IF LeadA_State THEN\n        IF NOT scanFaultA THEN\n            PumpCmdA := TRUE;\n            PumpCmdB := FALSE;\n        ELSIF NOT scanFaultB THEN\n            PumpCmdA := FALSE;\n            PumpCmdB := TRUE;\n        ELSE\n            PumpCmdA := FALSE;\n            PumpCmdB := FALSE;\n        END_IF;\n    ELSE\n        IF NOT scanFaultB THEN\n            PumpCmdA := FALSE;\n            PumpCmdB := TRUE;\n        ELSIF NOT scanFaultA THEN\n            PumpCmdA := TRUE;\n            PumpCmdB := FALSE;\n        ELSE\n            PumpCmdA := FALSE;\n            PumpCmdB := FALSE;\n        END_IF;\n    END_IF;\n    IF PumpCmdA OR PumpCmdB THEN\n        served := TRUE;\n    END_IF;\nEND_IF;\n\nprevious_demand := scanDemand;\n\nPumpA := PumpCmdA;\nPumpB := PumpCmdB;\nLeadA := LeadA_State;"

Need perhaps if Demand true and lead healthy but other fault? We run lead. At most one. Good.

Could code be simplified. Fine.

Need answer only JSON. No markdown. Ensure top-level has declaration, implementation, supporting_objects. For supporting_objects empty array. Good.

Double-check initial values: output LeadA := TRUE. PumpA/PumpB false. Internal LeadA_State true, previous false, served false. PumpCmd false. Good. `scanDemand` etc default false. Fine.

Potential issue: CODESYS requires output variable initialization maybe at declaration after type: `LeadA : BOOL := TRUE;`. Good.

Potential issue: `served` and `episode_served` in initial values. We use served. They mention episode_served maybe synonym. Fine.

Potential issue: Requirements initial `LeadA := TRUE`, episode memory `served := FALSE`, previous_demand := FALSE. Good.

Need maybe use `VAR RETAIN`? No.

Potential issue: "ommit END_FUNCTION_BLOCK" in declaration. We do. Implementation body alone. Good.

Potential issue: all VAR sections included. Good.

Let's final.
